articleTitle: Battery state of charge measurement or estimation
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Vehicle Electrical Power Management and Smart Alternators
abstract: The number of electronic functions and components built into cars have increased on an exponential basis. Along with the engine starting and car lighting functions, there are now a multitude of other electrical components. These include components related to the basic driving functions, and others which make driving more comfortable. The importance of the battery within the car has increased correspondingly. Parallel to that development, considerable optimisation of the battery has been engineered. The author provides the relevant battery information. The connection between the state of charge of the battery, the specific gravity of the electrolyte and the voltage-in relation to all of the demands within the vehicle. The resulting possible methods of measuring or assessing this information are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Vehicle Electrical Power Management and Smart Alternators' (Digest No.53)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Vehicle Electrical Power Management and Smart Alternators
IEE Colloquium on Vehicle Electrical Power Management and Smart Alternators
abstract: The polymer battery has opened up a whole new field of research. Whilst it will certainly not replace the lead acid accumulator-it is however a real alternative for other rechargeable battery systems in the consumer battery field. With further increased electronics within the motor car this polymer battery is also interesting as regards a separate power supply. The author discusses four main points: characteristics and construction of polymers; conductivity polymers; electrochemistry of conductivity polymers; and features of cells with polymer electrodes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Vehicle Electrical Power Management and Smart Alternators
abstract: Lucas are active in the design and specification of vehicle electrical power systems. It is required that the charging and storage system should be adequate for the demands placed on it during vehicle use. As the pace of change increases, and as weight and cost constraints tighten, it becomes necessary to assess proposed systems quickly, cheaply, and reliably before implementing in hardware. To this end a computer simulation model has been developed by the Lucas Research Centre, sponsored by other Lucas companies. The purpose of the simulation model is to predict the performance of an automotive electrical power system when exercised by a variety of duty cycles. The performance is defined by the system voltages at specific points (e.g. battery terminals, electronic control module), current flows between specific points (e.g. into/out of battery), and by state of charge (SOC) of the storage element. The model and its application are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New concepts for vehicle electrical systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Vehicle Electrical Power Management and Smart Alternators
abstract: The electric power consumption of passenger cars is increasing rapidly. The principle reasons are new electrical devices for comfort and security. This makes an improvement of alternator output performance and the development of new vehicle electrical systems necessary to cover future requirements. More powerful alternators can be achieved by increasing the active volume and the specific utilisation. But what about the vehicle electrical system? A change to higher voltages, even in passenger cars, and totally new structures such as multiple voltage systems have to be considered. The authors discuss the advantages of using 24 V instead of 12 V for the electrical system. They then briefly discuss the components of a multiple voltage electrical system including the bidirectional DC/DC converter, heatable front windscreen, and 3-phase PWM converter with flywheel starter/alternator.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Batteries for new concepts of electrical systems in passenger cars
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Vehicle Electrical Power Management and Smart Alternators
abstract: When forced to redesign the electrical network of future passenger cars because of new demands on electrical energy, the opportunity should be taken to think about how new degrees of freedom in battery design could be used to raise the reliability of the whole system. The author discusses the battery and related components requirements for such a future passenger car. They conclude that the whole electrical system and not just individual parts, should be improved.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Vehicle Electrical Power Management and Smart Alternators
abstract: The author discusses the need to change to a higher voltage than 12 V for cars. He goes on to discuss the possibility of using AC systems, concluding that they are not suitable except for special purposes. The author then goes on to discuss the choice of DC voltage systems, in particular generation, storage, engine starting, distribution, control, and utilisation. The use of a dual 42/12 V system and the alternator for such a system are also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The size of batteries to come
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Vehicle Electrical Power Management and Smart Alternators
abstract: The lead acid battery's ability to provide a long and efficient service life for a car depends partly on it being maintained at a reasonably high state of charge. However, this is not always possible due to the major factors of the charging circuit and the growth of the quiescent load. The author concentrates on these two aspects, discussing the battery rating, state of charge, battery charging and dual systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Semiconductor devices for low standby current in automotive electronics
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Vehicle Electrical Power Management and Smart Alternators
abstract: In many automotive electronic systems there is a need to maintain a permanent battery fed connection: vehicle supervisory systems which may be activated upon entering the car, or the retention of data acquired during the operation of a system are examples. In such systems, the total current flow through any device left connected to the power supply of the vehicle must be kept to an absolute minimum. The author examines how the use of some semiconductor devices can reduce standby current in various automotive systems. He discusses CMOS technology, microcontrollers, data storage, voltage regulators, remote locking systems and intelligent power switches.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
